analysis:
Documentation-only changes. docs/developer/test.md head lines 1048-1059 and 1066-1078 now describe the dev-branch release lane (.github/workflows/release-dev-branch.yml) as triggered only by pushes to `dev`, with no dispatch, input or `ref:`. It calls release-provider.yml with environment dev and `secrets: inherit`. The description says Apple signing secrets are read only in the signing job and that a master push publishes staging only when STAGING_ENABLED is true. docs/operations/provider-release.md (metadata unit only; the patch excerpt is truncated) states that master no longer publishes dev releases.

The security-relevant shift versus the base doc: the dev lane was previously described as having no signing identity or secret and publishing only with DEV_RELEASE_KEY. It now inherits secrets, including the five Apple Developer ID signing secrets, on any push to `dev`. That widens who can produce Developer ID-signed artifacts to anyone with push access to `dev`. This bears on A-011/A-017 (official-build identity and qualification), T-013/T-054 (signed build accepted) and A-005 (release registration key).

The docs assert dev-scope isolation through environment `dev`, a verified commit on dev ancestry, and the resolver refusing staging/prod. A Developer ID signature alone does not grant qualification per TB-011/T-054. These are doc claims; the workflow YAML, release-provider.yml secret guards, branch protection on `dev` and the test scripts were not supplied. I cannot verify whether a dev-signed artifact can be registered or qualified outside the dev environment.

Integration should examine:
- .github/workflows/release-dev-branch.yml and release-provider.yml: secret scoping by environment.
- Whether GitHub environment `dev` protection restricts the Apple signing secrets.
- Whether dev-signed builds share the Apple team requirement checked by the self-updater (test.md:1078), since a dev-branch build could satisfy the updater's designated requirement.

No concrete regression is visible in the supplied evidence; this is flagged for deeper review.
